title: Ownership limits on major airports
summary: The Airports Act 1996 limits airline ownership of airport-operator companies and cross-ownership of airports.
direction_rationale: Ownership limits restrict who may own an airport operator.

industries.name: Airport Operations and Other Air Transport Support Services

verified.notes: An existing setting: no dates. The requirement inside it quotes the airline-ownership rule.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 17 November 2026 (phase 6 of the levers re-evaluation, batch 1) from the law quoted. Not yet checked: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: Airlines may own no more than a small share of a major airport's operator, and the Sydney airports may not be owned together. The limits stop airlines controlling the airports their rivals use, and stop one owner holding every Sydney airport; they also narrow who may invest.

marks.reason: Keeps airlines from controlling the airports their rivals depend on.
Narrows the owners who may invest in a major airport.

assessment.confidence_note: The limits protect competition between airlines while limiting investment; the marks offset.
